# What this document does

Two SEIR BiLSTM models, both the average of 5 seeds, read the same 61-day windows:

- **SEIR v2** (`SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd`, `results/seir_bilstm_v2`): trained only on the first
  61 days of simulated epidemics. Besides `ptran`, `crate` and `R0` it estimates the
  share initially exposed (`preval`); everyone else starts susceptible.
- **Variable-length v3** (`SEIR_variable_length_BiLSTM.Rmd`,
  `results/seir_variable_length_v3`): trained on windows of 30 to 365 days from the
  beginning, middle and end of 365-day epidemics. Besides `ptran`, `crate` and `R0` it
  estimates the shares exposed, infectious and recovered on the first day of the window.

Both get the same known values (`n`, `recov`, `incub`). The windows:

1. **Utah COVID-19 data (last 365 days):** the first 61 days (beginning), the middle 61
   days and the last 61 days (end), then every 61-day window starting every
   `r params$step` days. There is no true R0 for real data, so each model's estimates
   are run `r params$n_reps` times through the SEIR simulator, starting from the
   model's own estimate of the starting state, and scored by how much of the observed
   curve falls inside the 95% band.
2. **Simulated epidemics (true R0 known):** the 61-day windows at the beginning, middle
   and end of the test epidemics in the v3 report (the same windows, so the v3 numbers
   match that report).

To run it (from the `examples/` folder):

```r
rmarkdown::render("Compare_SEIR_v2_v3_windows.Rmd", output_dir = "results/seir_v2_vs_v3_windows")
```

# Setup

```{r packages}
pkgload::load_all("..", quiet = TRUE)
if (nzchar(params$condaenv)) {
  reticulate::use_condaenv(params$condaenv, required = TRUE)
}
reticulate::py_run_string(paste(
  "import warnings",
  "from sklearn.exceptions import InconsistentVersionWarning",
  "warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=InconsistentVersionWarning)",
  sep = "\n"
))
```

```{r settings}
OUT_DIR <- params$out_dir
WINDOW  <- params$window
N_REPS  <- params$n_reps
KNOWN   <- c("n", "recov", "incub")
STATE_NAMES <- c("exposed_share", "infected_share", "recovered_share")
POSITIONS   <- c("beginning", "middle", "end")
UTAH_N <- 5000; UTAH_RECOV <- 1 / 7; UTAH_INCUB <- params$utah_incub

dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(OUT_DIR), "figures", ""))

# Several seeds = average of their estimates, with crate recomputed from the
# averaged ptran and R0 (as in both reports).
make_model <- function(dirs) {
  cls <- lapply(trimws(strsplit(dirs, ",")[[1]]), function(d)
    bilstm_calibrator(d, known_names = KNOWN, type = "SEIR", device = params$device))
  if (length(cls) == 1) return(cls[[1]])
  structure(list(
    pre_process  = function(x, ...) x,
    run          = function(x, ...) rowMeans(sapply(cls, function(cl) calibrate(x, cl, ...))),
    post_process = function(x, recov = NULL, ...) derive_crate(x, recov = recov),
    type         = "SEIR"
  ), class = "calibrator")
}
models <- list(`SEIR v2` = make_model(params$v2_models),
               `Variable-length v3` = make_model(params$v3_models))
MODEL_COLS <- c(`SEIR v2` = "darkorange", `Variable-length v3` = "purple")

# Where a 61-day window starts inside `last` days.
window_start <- function(position, last) {
  switch(position, beginning = 1, middle = floor((last - WINDOW) / 2) + 1, end = last - WINDOW + 1)
}

cuda_ok <- reticulate::py_eval("__import__('torch').cuda.is_available()")
device  <- if (params$device == "cpu" || !cuda_ok) "cpu" else "cuda"
cat("BiLSTM predictions on:", device, "\n")
```

# Utah COVID-19 data

```{r utah-data}
utah <- read.csv(file.path(params$v3_run, "utah_covid_last365days.csv"))
utah$Date <- as.Date(utah$Date)
write.csv(utah, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_covid_last365days.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

main_starts <- vapply(POSITIONS, window_start, numeric(1), last = nrow(utah))
starts <- sort(unique(c(seq(1, nrow(utah) - WINDOW + 1, by = params$step), main_starts)))
cat("Dates:", format(min(utah$Date)), "to", format(max(utah$Date)), "|",
    length(starts), "windows of", WINDOW, "days\n")
```

```{r utah-plot-data, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.5}
plot(utah$Date, utah$Daily.Cases, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue", xlab = "",
     ylab = "daily cases", main = "Utah, last 365 days: the three main 61-day windows")
for (k in seq_along(POSITIONS)) {
  s <- main_starts[k]
  rect(utah$Date[s], par("usr")[3], utah$Date[s + WINDOW - 1], par("usr")[4],
       col = adjustcolor("grey50", 0.2), border = NA)
  text(utah$Date[s + WINDOW %/% 2], par("usr")[4], POSITIONS[k], pos = 1)
}
```

## Fitting each window

Each model's estimates are simulated `r N_REPS` times (seeds 1 to `r N_REPS`), with
`n = 5000`, `recov = 1/7`, `incub = `r UTAH_INCUB``, as in both reports. The starting
state is each model's own estimate:

- **SEIR v2:** `preval` exposed, everyone else susceptible (a fresh epidemic);
- **Variable-length v3:** the estimated shares exposed, infectious and recovered.

Coverage is the share of observed days inside the 95% band; RMSE and MAE compare the
median simulated curve with the observed cases.

```{r utah-fit}
sim <- seir_simulator(ndays = WINDOW)

start_state <- function(est) {
  if (all(STATE_NAMES %in% names(est))) {
    list(preval = est[["exposed_share"]], start_infected = est[["infected_share"]],
         start_recovered = est[["recovered_share"]])
  } else {
    list(preval = est[["preval"]])
  }
}

band <- function(est) {
  pars <- c(list(n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB,
                 ptran = est[["ptran"]], crate = est[["crate"]]), start_state(est))
  runs <- vapply(seq_len(N_REPS), function(i) simulate_from_parameters(sim, pars, seed = i),
                 numeric(WINDOW))
  data.frame(day = seq_len(WINDOW), median = apply(runs, 1, median),
             lower = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.025), upper = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.975))
}

fits <- list()
rolling <- do.call(rbind, lapply(starts, function(s) {
  y <- utah$Daily.Cases[s:(s + WINDOW - 1)]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(m) {
    est <- calibrate(y, models[[m]], n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB)
    b   <- band(est)
    fits[[paste(m, s)]] <<- list(est = est, band = b, y = y)
    data.frame(
      model = m, window_start = s, first_date = utah$Date[s], last_date = utah$Date[s + WINDOW - 1],
      position = if (s %in% main_starts) names(main_starts)[match(s, main_starts)] else "",
      R0 = est[["R0"]], ptran = est[["ptran"]], crate = est[["crate"]],
      preval = if ("preval" %in% names(est)) est[["preval"]] else NA,
      exposed_share   = if ("exposed_share" %in% names(est)) est[["exposed_share"]] else NA,
      infected_share  = if ("infected_share" %in% names(est)) est[["infected_share"]] else NA,
      recovered_share = if ("recovered_share" %in% names(est)) est[["recovered_share"]] else NA,
      coverage_pct = 100 * mean(y >= b$lower & y <= b$upper),
      RMSE = sqrt(mean((b$median - y)^2)),
      MAE  = mean(abs(b$median - y))
    )
  }))
}))
write.csv(rolling, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_all_windows.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Beginning, middle and end

```{r utah-main-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
op <- par(mfrow = c(length(models), length(POSITIONS)), mar = c(4, 4, 3.5, 1))
for (m in names(models)) {
  for (pos in POSITIONS) {
    s  <- main_starts[[pos]]
    f  <- fits[[paste(m, s)]]
    dates <- utah$Date[s:(s + WINDOW - 1)]
    # Same y-axis for both models in a window.
    ylim <- range(unlist(lapply(names(models), function(mm) {
      ff <- fits[[paste(mm, s)]]; c(ff$y, ff$band$lower, ff$band$upper)
    })))
    r <- rolling[rolling$model == m & rolling$window_start == s, ]
    plot(dates, f$band$median, type = "n", ylim = ylim, xlab = "", ylab = "daily cases",
         main = sprintf("%s, %s\nR0 %.2f | coverage %.0f%%", m, pos, r$R0, r$coverage_pct))
    polygon(c(dates, rev(dates)), c(f$band$upper, rev(f$band$lower)),
            col = adjustcolor(MODEL_COLS[[m]], alpha.f = 0.3), border = NA)
    lines(dates, f$band$median, col = MODEL_COLS[[m]], lwd = 2)
    lines(dates, f$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
    points(dates, f$y, col = "blue", pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
  }
}
par(op)
```

```{r utah-main-table}
main_tab <- rolling[rolling$position != "", ]
main_tab <- main_tab[order(match(main_tab$position, POSITIONS), main_tab$model), ]
main_tab$dates <- paste(format(main_tab$first_date), "to", format(main_tab$last_date))
write.csv(main_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_beginning_middle_end.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(main_tab[, c("position", "dates", "model", "R0", "coverage_pct", "RMSE", "MAE")],
             digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("window", "dates", "model", "R0", "coverage %", "RMSE", "MAE"))
```

The starting state each model assumed (shares of the population):

```{r utah-start-state}
knitr::kable(main_tab[, c("position", "model", "preval", "exposed_share", "infected_share",
                          "recovered_share", "ptran", "crate")],
             digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Every 61-day window

All `r length(starts)` windows starting every `r params$step` days (the three main
windows are marked with dashed lines):

```{r utah-rolling-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (what in c("R0", "coverage_pct")) {
  plot(range(rolling$first_date), range(c(0, rolling[[what]])), type = "n",
       xlab = "first day of the 61-day window", ylab = if (what == "R0") "estimated R0" else "coverage %",
       main = if (what == "R0") "R0 estimate" else "Observed days inside the 95% band")
  abline(v = utah$Date[main_starts], lty = 2, col = "grey50")
  for (m in names(models)) {
    r <- rolling[rolling$model == m, ]
    lines(r$first_date, r[[what]], type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = MODEL_COLS[[m]])
  }
  legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = MODEL_COLS, legend = names(models))
}
par(op)
```

```{r utah-rolling-summary}
wide <- reshape(rolling[, c("model", "window_start", "coverage_pct")], idvar = "window_start",
                timevar = "model", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("coverage_pct.", "", names(wide), fixed = TRUE)
utah_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(m) {
  r <- rolling[rolling$model == m, ]
  other <- setdiff(names(models), m)
  data.frame(model = m, windows = nrow(r),
             mean_coverage_pct = mean(r$coverage_pct), median_coverage_pct = median(r$coverage_pct),
             mean_RMSE = mean(r$RMSE),
             windows_with_higher_coverage = sum(wide[[m]] > wide[[other]]),
             R0_min = min(r$R0), R0_max = max(r$R0))
}))
write.csv(utah_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_all_windows_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(utah_summary, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Simulated epidemics (true R0 known)

The 61-day windows from the v3 report: the first 61 days (beginning), the middle and
the last 61 days of each test epidemic's informative days (before its first week
without cases). SEIR v2 was only trained on the beginning.

```{r sim-windows}
test_dir  <- file.path(params$v3_run, "test_bank")
test_bank <- read_training_data(file.path(test_dir, "seir_theta.csv"),
                                file.path(test_dir, "seir_observations.csv"), type = "SEIR")
grid <- read.csv(file.path(params$v3_run, "grid_estimates.csv"))
win  <- unique(grid[grid$length == WINDOW, c("curve", "position", "window_start")])
win  <- win[order(match(win$position, POSITIONS), win$curve), ]
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(position = factor(win$position, POSITIONS)), responseName = "windows"))
```

```{r sim-estimates}
sim_est <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(m) {
  t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  r0 <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(win)), function(k) {
    i <- win$curve[k]; s <- win$window_start[k]
    calibrate(as.numeric(test_bank$observations[i, s:(s + WINDOW - 1)]), models[[m]],
              n = test_bank$theta$n[i], recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i],
              incub = test_bank$theta$incub[i])[["R0"]]
  }, numeric(1))
  data.frame(model = m, win, R0 = r0, R0_true = test_bank$theta$R0[win$curve],
             seconds_per_window = (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0) / nrow(win))
}))
sim_est$R0_abs_error <- abs(sim_est$R0 - sim_est$R0_true)
write.csv(sim_est, file.path(OUT_DIR, "simulated_estimates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

sim_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(m) do.call(rbind, lapply(POSITIONS, function(pos) {
  g <- sim_est[sim_est$model == m & sim_est$position == pos, ]
  data.frame(model = m, position = pos, R0_MAE = mean(g$R0_abs_error),
             R0_R2 = 1 - sum((g$R0 - g$R0_true)^2) / sum((g$R0_true - mean(g$R0_true))^2),
             R0_bias = mean(g$R0 - g$R0_true))
}))))
write.csv(sim_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "simulated_R0_by_position.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(sim_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r sim-scatter, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
lim <- range(c(sim_est$R0, sim_est$R0_true))
op <- par(mfrow = c(length(models), length(POSITIONS)), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (m in names(models)) {
  for (pos in POSITIONS) {
    g <- sim_est[sim_est$model == m & sim_est$position == pos, ]
    plot(g$R0_true, g$R0, xlim = lim, ylim = lim, pch = 16, cex = 0.6,
         col = adjustcolor(MODEL_COLS[[m]], 0.6), xlab = "true R0", ylab = "estimated R0",
         main = sprintf("%s, %s (MAE %.3f)", m, pos, mean(g$R0_abs_error)))
    abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
  }
}
par(op)
```

```{r sim-time}
knitr::kable(aggregate(seconds_per_window ~ model, sim_est, mean), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = paste("Seconds per 61-day window (5-seed average), predictions on", device))
```

# Summary

```{r summary}
summary_tab <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(POSITIONS, function(pos) {
    r <- main_tab[main_tab$position == pos, ]
    data.frame(measure = paste("Utah", pos, "window: coverage %"),
               `SEIR v2` = r$coverage_pct[r$model == "SEIR v2"],
               `Variable-length v3` = r$coverage_pct[r$model == "Variable-length v3"], check.names = FALSE)
  })),
  data.frame(measure = sprintf("Utah, all %d windows: mean coverage %%", length(starts)),
             `SEIR v2` = utah_summary$mean_coverage_pct[utah_summary$model == "SEIR v2"],
             `Variable-length v3` = utah_summary$mean_coverage_pct[utah_summary$model == "Variable-length v3"],
             check.names = FALSE),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(POSITIONS, function(pos) {
    r <- sim_tab[sim_tab$position == pos, ]
    data.frame(measure = paste("Simulated", pos, "windows: R0 MAE"),
               `SEIR v2` = r$R0_MAE[r$model == "SEIR v2"],
               `Variable-length v3` = r$R0_MAE[r$model == "Variable-length v3"], check.names = FALSE)
  }))
)
summary_tab$better <- ifelse(grepl("coverage", summary_tab$measure),
  ifelse(summary_tab$`SEIR v2` > summary_tab$`Variable-length v3`, "SEIR v2",
         ifelse(summary_tab$`SEIR v2` < summary_tab$`Variable-length v3`, "Variable-length v3", "tie")),
  ifelse(summary_tab$`SEIR v2` < summary_tab$`Variable-length v3`, "SEIR v2", "Variable-length v3"))
write.csv(summary_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

Notes:

- Coverage on Utah measures how well the simulated curves match the data, not whether
  R0 is right; the simulated windows check R0 against the truth.
- SEIR v2 always assumes a fresh epidemic (no one recovered at the window start); v3
  estimates the recovered share, which only matters if earlier infections slowed the
  epidemic down.
